What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We map the user and customer journey from signup to renewal with the founder and the product, revenue and support leads, audit the event taxonomy, billing setup and CRM hygiene, and trace where personal data flows. We then pick one workflow where a clear signal already exists and an owner is ready to act on it.

    Deliverables

    • Journey and event audit with gaps
    • Personal data map for the workflows in scope
    • Prioritized automation backlog with proposed KPIs
    • Pilot proposal with owner, scope and success measures

    What we need from you

    • Read access to PostHog or your analytics tool, Stripe or Razorpay, the CRM and the help desk
    • Time with the founder and the product, revenue and support leads
    • Current privacy policy, consent notices and terms of service
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We specify events, scoring rules, message matrices, review queues and escalation paths, and write down every human checkpoint and stop condition. For AI features we agree the evaluation rubric, confidence thresholds and disclosure wording before anything is built.

    Deliverables

    • Event and scoring specification
    • Message matrix with caps, quiet hours and stop rules
    • Human checkpoint and escalation map
    • Evaluation rubric and threshold proposal for AI features

    What we need from you

    • Approval of activation, qualification and risk definitions
    • Renewal, cancellation and AI disclosure wording reviewed by your legal or compliance owner
    • Brand voice guidelines and example messages
  3. 3

    Build

    2–4 weeks

    We build in your accounts: n8n workflows, PostHog destinations, CRM objects, Retool queues, retrieval indexes and dashboards, starting in Stripe test mode and CRM sandboxes. Every workflow gets logging, failure alerts and a feature-flag kill switch.

    Deliverables

    • Workflows and queues in a staging environment
    • Integrations and secrets set up in your accounts
    • Failure alerting and run logs
    • A runbook for each workflow

    What we need from you

    • Sandbox or test accounts for billing, CRM and help desk
    • API credentials shared through a secrets manager
    • WhatsApp message templates submitted for Meta approval where WhatsApp is used
    • Current help docs and policy pages
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    We test with seeded accounts and replayed events, run AI features in shadow mode where drafts are reviewed but not sent, keep a holdout group for nudges, and release behind feature flags to a first segment before widening.

    Deliverables

    • Test plan and results
    • Shadow-mode review report for AI features
    • Staged rollout plan with rollback steps
    • Training for owners and reviewers

    What we need from you

    • Named testers from sales, success and support
    • Go-live sign-off from each workflow owner
    • Reviewer time during shadow mode
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Monthly, ongoing

    We watch failures and queue ages, compare KPIs with the baseline and holdout each month, tune thresholds and messages, refresh knowledge sources and evaluation sets, and review access and data retention every quarter.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and exception review
    • Change log for thresholds, rules and prompts
    • Quarterly access and retention review
    • Backlog of next workflows

    What we need from you

    • Owner attendance at the monthly review
    • Feedback from account executives, success managers and reviewers
    • Advance notice of pricing, plan or policy changes

First pilot: Product-signal routing pilot

A pilot of four to six weeks on one segment: one activation milestone with stuck-step messages, one product-qualified rule routed to account executives with a brief, and one renewal-risk alert for customer success. We agree a baseline first, with a holdout group where volumes allow, so the result is judged on your own numbers rather than on estimates.

  • Event taxonomy cleanup for the activation path in PostHog
  • Stuck-step messages by email and in-product, with caps and stop rules
  • One product-qualified rule creating CRM tasks with Slack briefs
  • One weekly renewal-risk alert for customer success
  • Baseline, holdout group and a weekly calibration session

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • Every workflow has a named business owner, a runbook, failure alerts in Slack and a feature-flag kill switch that stops sends without a deploy.
  • Messages check consent, channel preference, frequency caps and quiet hours before sending and stop on conversion, opt-out or cancellation; trial, renewal and cancellation flows are reviewed against India's dark patterns guidelines.
  • AI drafts, classifies, summarizes and routes; people decide refunds, pricing, account actions, moderation outcomes and anything sent to investors. Chat assistants disclose that they are AI at the first message.
  • Data minimization by default: workspace-level aggregates for sales and success, redaction of secrets and payment data before model calls, and providers set not to train on client data where that option exists.
  • Least-privilege service accounts, secrets kept in a manager rather than inside workflows, and audit logs on any queue that shows identity documents or user content.
  • Prompts, scoring rules, templates and evaluation sets are versioned in GitHub, and each change passes the evaluation gate or a named reviewer before release.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • India's DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025, plus GDPR for EU users

    The DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases: consent manager rules from November 2026 and most duties from May 2027, including standalone consent notices, security safeguards, breach intimation to the Data Protection Board and affected users, and verifiable parental consent for users under 18, with limits on tracking children. EU users add GDPR duties such as a lawful basis per purpose and processor contracts. Tracking and AI features stay within each notice.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • RBI e-mandate framework for recurring payments

    Recurring card, UPI and prepaid-instrument payments in India run on e-mandates under the RBI's Digital Payments E-mandate Framework, 2026: one-time registration with additional authentication, an issuer notice at least 24 hours before each debit with an opt-out, and additional authentication for debits above ₹15,000. Recovery flows for Indian customers therefore bring people back to authenticate instead of retrying silently.

    rbi.org.in · Source

  • Dark patterns guidelines for trials, renewals and cancellation

    India's Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 apply to platforms offering goods or services in India and list subscription traps, nagging, confirm shaming and SaaS billing practices such as converting a free trial to paid without notice. From 1 January 2027, the amended E-Commerce Rules also require e-commerce entities to self-audit for dark patterns every year. We review trial, renewal and cancellation flows against these lists.

    consumeraffairs.gov.in · Source

  • Commercial email and messaging consent

    The US CAN-SPAM Act covers all commercial email, including business-to-business: accurate headers and subject lines, a valid postal address and an opt-out honored within 10 business days. WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy requires opt-in before messaging and clear escalation to a human when automation answers. Lifecycle workflows check these preferences before every send.

    ftc.gov · Source

  • Platform duties under India's IT Rules and app store policies

    Platforms hosting user content are intermediaries under India's IT Rules, amended in February 2026: publish a grievance officer, acknowledge complaints within 24 hours, resolve them within seven days, act faster on specified categories and label AI-generated content made with their tools. Apple's guidelines require filtering, reporting and blocking for user content, and explicit permission before personal data is shared with third-party AI.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • EU AI Act transparency for chatbots and generated content

    Article 50 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026: AI systems that interact with people must make clear they are AI unless that is obvious, and providers of generative systems must mark outputs in a machine-readable way, with a short transition for systems already on the market. The 2026 Digital Omnibus postponed the high-risk rules but kept the chatbot disclosure date. Assistants we build for EU users disclose AI at the first message.

    ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu · Source

Frequently asked

We are an early-stage startup with a small team. Where should we start?

With one workflow where a signal already exists and someone is ready to act on it, usually activation nudges, product-qualified routing or failed-payment recovery. A pilot runs four to six weeks in your own accounts, and you decide on the next workflow after seeing results against your own baseline.

Do we need to replace our CRM, help desk or billing system?

No. We connect what you already use, such as HubSpot or Salesforce, Intercom or Freshdesk, and Stripe or Razorpay, and add n8n workflows, Retool queues or small services only where a gap exists. Everything runs in accounts you own.

Our customers are in India and pay by card or UPI. Does payment recovery work differently?

Yes. Recurring Indian card and UPI payments run on RBI e-mandates, with a bank notice before each debit and additional authentication above ₹15,000, and Stripe attempts India-issued card renewals only once. Recovery therefore focuses on bringing customers back to authenticate or switch payment method, with clear transactional messages, rather than on repeated retries.

Will an AI assistant answer our customers on its own?

Only for questions your approved docs can answer, with citations and a clear statement that it is an AI. Refunds, billing disputes, account access, security reports, data requests and anything it is unsure about go to your team with a summary. You approve the sources and review samples before its scope grows.

How do you handle the DPDP Act and GDPR?

We map the personal data each workflow touches, minimize it, and design notices, consent checks, retention and access around it. For B2B products we also separate the data you control about your own users from the data you process on behalf of your customers. Your legal or compliance owner reviews notices and decisions; this is design support, not legal advice.

Can you help us with SOC 2 or ISO 27001?

MoreSpace is not an auditor and does not certify anyone. For the automations we build, we document data flows, access, change control and logs, which your team and your chosen auditor can use as evidence within your own program.

Who owns the workflows, prompts and code after handover?

You do. Workflows, prompts, evaluation sets and code live in your accounts and your GitHub organization, with runbooks so your team can operate them. We can stay on for monthly operation and improvement or hand over fully.

How do you show results without inventing numbers?

We record a baseline before launch, keep holdout groups for nudges where volumes allow, and report agreed KPIs such as activation, trial-to-paid conversion, payment recovery and response time from your own systems. If a workflow does not move its measure, we change it or retire it.
